neighbours.label: a word saying a condition is present but latent, not yet surfaced (lie dormant, latent period, stay hidden, simmer beneath the surface), as against the condition being overt or the same verbs used literally
fire: After the chickenpox clears, the virus can remain dormant in nerve cells for decades.
Tension between the two brothers had been quietly simmering beneath their polite smiles.
Some heart conditions remain hidden for years without any warning signs.
Tuberculosis often stays latent in the lungs until the immune system weakens.
Seeds of the desert flower lie dormant in the sand until the rains come.
Resentment over the merger kept smouldering beneath the surface at the office.
Early glaucoma is a silent disease that hides behind normal eyesight for a long time.
Mould spores can remain dormant inside the walls until the house gets damp.
quiet: After the chickenpox cleared, the child went back to school on Monday.
The two brothers shouted at each other in front of all the guests.
Some heart conditions cause sudden chest pain and shortness of breath.
Tuberculosis causes a heavy cough, fever and night sweats in many patients.
The desert flower blooms bright red within days of the spring rains.
Staff at the office openly protested the merger on the front steps.
His glaucoma was diagnosed at a routine eye exam last spring.
Black mould spread across the bathroom ceiling in plain sight.
